item.title: Opinion: Trump’s South Caucasus diplomacy revives sanctions question over Georgia
item.description: The US vice-president will not visit Georgia during his February trip to the South Caucasus

item.title: Yerevan discusses the potential for linking energy systems of Armenia and Azerbaijan
item.description: The debate was prompted by a statement from Nikol Pashinyan: “The energy systems of Armenia and Azerbaijan will be linked and will make mutual use of export and import opportunities.”

item.title: Ex-Russian official detained in Georgia at Moscow’s request despite cancelled Interpol notice
item.description: Mikhail Timofeev, an aide to the former governor of Russia’s Khabarovsk region, sought political asylum in Georgia, citing persecution by the Russian authorities.

item.title: Iran unrest: Washington Post weighs possible Baku move to protect ethnic Azeris
item.description: Around 20 million ethnic Azerbaijanis live in Iran — more than in Azerbaijan itself. They make up about 23% of Iran’s population.

item.title: UN rapporteur on situation in Georgia: ‘New laws amount to systematic pressure on civil society’
item.description: According to Mary Lawlor, policies pursued by the Georgian authorities in recent years have significantly narrowed the space for human rights protection.

item.title: Former deputy health minister detained in Georgia
item.description: He is accused of abusing his official powers in order to obtain illegal income.

item.title: Russia provides Abkhazia with additional free electricity for February
item.description: This means that rolling power cuts in Abkhazia are unlikely this winter.

item.title: ‘Abkhazia is not anyone’s showcase, and we did not ask Moscow for help’ — response to Russian propagandist’s article
item.description: Public figure Akhra Bzhaniya says it is unjust and futile to demand “feudal submission” from Abkhazia.

item.title: Partial reopening of Armenia–Turkey border expected, no date announced yet
item.description: According to Armenian media, the border will open on 1 February for third-country nationals and holders of diplomatic passports. Official Yerevan has neither confirmed nor denied these reports.
